newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends up ahead of FOMC meeting.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends up ahead of FOMC meeting.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed up 120 basis points at 18.20 percent on Monday from what traders said was an unrepresentative low prior close.
Dealing was cautious and rates subject to some upside pressure, however, on uncertainty ahead of Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee meeting to determine U.S. interest rates, traders said.
"Everybody is waiting for the FOMC meeting," a fixed-income analyst said, adding the market had largely discounted a 25-basis-point hike in U.S. base rates.
"That is why dealing was quiet," he said.
Government rates traded in a narrow range of between 18.20-18.50 percent, dealers said.
"The market was very quiet and the only thing making some impact is the run up to the FOMC meeting," a dealer said.
Another analyst said concerns over the FOMC meeting had cushioned the potentially beneficial effect of strong GDP data released at mid-session.
"It was a mixed situation. GDP was good, the peso a little stronger, capital did flow inwards, but it was also on hold with the FOMC coming up tomorrow," he said.
The Finance Ministry announced Mexico's GDP grew by 5.1 percent in year-ago terms during the first quarter of 1997.
As opposed to developed markets, strong GDP data in Mexico are not seen as a symptom of overheating, but as a welcome sign of economic recovery.
Banco de Mexico drained 2.368 billion pesos from the market by assigning three direct Cetes sales and three repos.
Overnight rates on bank paper mirrored the trend on government rates and closed up 30 basis points at 19.50 percent.
Cetes futures traded on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange fell 10 centavos to 78.52 pesos for June contracts.
Liquidity of 136 million pesos was due to return to the system on Tuesday from prior central bank participation.
